question: Does the indexed 2009 conference abstract establish a usable fish record or a waterbody-level record for Malagaylay, Quezon?

findings.bibliographicCitation: Padalhin, A. R., Sales, A., Corpuz, M. N., Lontoc, B. M., Matalog, O. E., Labatos, B. V., Jr., & Ocampo, P. P. (2009, November 4–6). Evaluation of some biological parameters of an unidentified goby fish collected from Malagaylay, Quezon Province (Abstract). 13th Southern Luzon Zonal R&D Symposium cum Aquatic Technology Road Show, PCAMRD Southern Luzon Zonal Center, Partido State University, Goa, Camarines Sur.
findings.retrieval: The DOST-STII SPHERES December 2018 bibliography lists the conference abstract. ResearchGate supplies matching title, conference and author metadata, but explicitly says no full text is available. Neither page provides the abstract body or data table.
findings.sourceLocality: The source title says only Malagaylay, Quezon Province. A search surfaced a third-party Scribd copy of a Tayabas City planning document that places Malagaylay Falls in Barangay Lalo; this is contextual retrieval evidence, not the study's station description or an authoritative source-to-waterbody crosswalk.
findings.taxon: The title calls the specimen an unidentified goby. No genus or species name is supported by the reviewed material.
findings.reuse: No item-specific reuse license or permission for the 2009 abstract or underlying data was located. The DOST bibliography's availability does not grant reuse rights to the conference work.

interpretation: Retain this as a Quezon freshwater literature lead only; the abstract body, collection station, date, methods, sample size, diagnostic characters, voucher, and underlying data remain unavailable.
Do not assign the record to Malagaylay Falls, a stream, river, or Barangay Lalo solely from the shared place name.
Do not infer a species identity, present-day occurrence, abundance, habitat range, diet, or fishing suitability from the title.
The 2012 Tayabas planning-document copy is hosted on a third-party document-sharing site; its locality statement can guide future source retrieval but cannot resolve the specimen station.

additionalSearchLead.description: A third-party-hosted copy attributed to the Tayabas City Office of City Planning and Development Coordinator's 2012 Comprehensive Development Plan states that Malagaylay Falls is in Barangay Lalo. The source file has not been obtained from an official city repository, and no reviewed evidence ties the 2009 goby collection to the falls.
additionalSearchLead.disposition: Unverified locality context only; not admitted as a waterbody crosswalk, fish record, or geometry source.

nextActions: If the original proceedings or author-shared abstract becomes accessible, inspect its complete methods, station wording, date, sample size, taxonomic evidence, voucher deposition, and item-specific reuse terms.
Seek an official Tayabas City copy of the relevant planning/tourism material and a primary map or field note before linking Malagaylay to a named stream or falls.
Continue separate, site-resolved freshwater survey research for other Quezon rivers and lakes; keep the regional checklist incomplete.

sources.supports: DOST-STII bibliography citation for the 2009 conference abstract and its full author list; it does not expose the abstract text or underlying data.
Secondary bibliographic metadata and explicit notice that no full text is available.
